titlePl: Ósmoklasista: Życie społeczne — 36 haseł do gier LingoSpark
titleEn: Grade 8 English: Social Life — 36 terms for LingoSpark games
blurbPl: Dział Życie społeczne: społeczność, prawo, wolontariat, dobre maniery. Listy do gier LingoSpark.
blurbEn: Grade-8 Social life module: community, rules, volunteering, manners. Paste into LingoSpark games.

items.definitionEn: an organisation that helps people in need; giving help
items.example: Our class collected food for a local charity.

items.definitionEn: someone who works for no pay to help others
items.example: She is a volunteer at the animal shelter on Saturdays.

items.definitionEn: to give money or things to help a person or charity
items.example: We donate old clothes twice a year.

items.definitionEn: without a place to live
items.example: The shelter offers meals to homeless people.

items.definitionEn: the state of being extremely poor
items.example: The organisation fights poverty in the region.

items.definitionEn: an action that is against the law
items.example: Stealing a bike is a crime.

items.definitionEn: to take something that is not yours
items.example: Someone tried to steal a phone from the changing room.

items.definitionEn: a person who breaks into a building to steal
items.example: The burglar got in through an open window.

items.definitionEn: money you must pay as a punishment
items.example: You can get a fine for dropping litter.

items.definitionEn: the system of rules in a country
items.example: Everyone must follow the law.

items.definitionEn: to do what a rule or person tells you
items.example: Drivers must obey the speed limit.

items.definitionEn: things you are allowed to have or do by law
items.example: Human rights include education, safety and a fair trial.

items.definitionEn: an event when people vote for a leader or party
items.example: There will be an election for the student council.

items.definitionEn: to choose in an election; one choice
items.example: Students vote for class president in September.

items.definitionEn: the group of people who run a country
items.example: The government decided to build a new hospital.

items.definitionEn: a person who belongs to a country and has rights there
items.example: A good citizen cares about other people in the town.

items.definitionEn: the people who live in the same area
items.example: The community organised a clean-up of the park.

items.definitionEn: a public event where people show they disagree
items.example: Students held a protest about the new school rules.

items.definitionEn: planned actions to change people's opinions or raise money
items.example: Our campaign collected money for the animal shelter.

items.definitionEn: hurting someone again and again, with words or actions
items.example: The school has a clear policy against bullying.

items.definitionEn: bullying that happens on the internet or by phone
items.example: Cyberbullying can happen even when you are at home.

items.definitionEn: having the same rights and chances as others
items.example: Boys and girls should have equal chances in sport.

items.definitionEn: not right or not treating people the same
items.example: It is unfair to punish the whole class for one person.

items.definitionEn: to give practical help
items.example: Can you help out at the school fete on Saturday?

items.definitionEn: to collect money for a purpose
items.example: We want to raise money for new sports equipment.

items.definitionEn: buses, trains and trams that anyone can use
items.example: Public transport is cheaper than going by car.

items.definitionEn: cars and other vehicles on the road
items.example: There is always heavy traffic at eight in the morning.

items.definitionEn: a person walking in the street, not in a vehicle
items.example: Drivers must stop for a pedestrian on the crossing.

items.definitionEn: instructions that say what you may or may not do
items.example: Read the rules before you start the game.

items.definitionEn: having good manners; not rude
items.example: It is polite to say please and thank you.

items.definitionEn: not polite; speaking or acting in an unkind way
items.example: It is rude to interrupt when someone is talking.

items.definitionEn: a feeling that someone is valuable; to treat them that way
items.example: We should respect other people's opinions even if we disagree.

items.definitionEn: all the people of about the same age in society
items.example: The older generation remembers life without the internet.

items.definitionEn: a duty to deal with something or take care of it
items.example: It is your responsibility to walk the dog after school.

items.definitionEn: to act in a particular way, especially well or badly
items.example: Please behave during the school performance.

items.definitionEn: polite ways of speaking and acting
items.example: Good manners include holding the door for others.
